newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: TINY ZAMBIAN STOCK EXCHANGE HAS BIG AMBITIONS.
newsitem.headline: TINY ZAMBIAN STOCK EXCHANGE HAS BIG AMBITIONS.

text.p: Business may be slow today but Zambia's young stock exchange, banking on progress in the country's privatisation programme, has high hopes for the future.
The exchange, which has a market capitalisation of around $300 million and five listed companies, was set up in February 1994 as part of Zambia's economic reforms.
"When you look at the potential for this market to grow once we achieve stability, the potential is certainly enormous,'' general manager Charles Mate said in an interview.

Although the market capitalisation had decreased by almost half since the exchange opened, Mate said this was due to the Zambian stock market finding its true value and a considerable plunge of the local kwacha currency against the dollar.

"Given that there was no prior experience and knowledge of stock markets in Zambia, it has taken us almost two years to get our stock prices to come down to prices that are much more realistic,'' he said.
Mate said at least 20 more Zambian companies were candidates for the stock market -- 15 of them state-owned and due to be privatised.
Among them are the Zambian telecommunications company Zamtel and the country's banks and breweries.
"These are all big companies which are still to come into the stock market,'' he said.

After independence from Britain in 1964, the Zambian government nationalised about 80 percent of the country's economy -- including collieries, breweries and the largest company, Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd (ZCCM) .
The government began to privatise its assets through the Zambia Privatisation Agency in September 1992 and so far 140 companies or business units have been sold.
ZCCM is listed on the Paris bourse and has been listed as a "B'' share on the Lusaka exchange.
The latest addition was Zambia Sugar Plc in September and the share offer was 25 percent oversubscribed.
In the first 10 months of 1996, 1,122 share transactions took place. Some 166.7 million shares were sold and turnover was 2.56 billion kwacha ($1.97 million).
Mate said activity on the exchange was satisfactory but it fluctuated.
"Averages are very difficult. Last month we did a single transaction of 140 million shares, it was a transaction worth $1.2 million,'' he said.
More typical, though, was trading this week with daily turnover of around 50,000 kwacha -- less than $50.
